id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Point-to-point serial fabric: phys aggregated into narrow / wide ports, interconnected through edge and fanout expander devices into a SAS domain. Connections are routed by 64-bit SAS address; there is no shared parallel bus.

supported_topologies.name: Direct-attach
supported_topologies.description: Initiator port connected point-to-point to a target port (no expander).

supported_topologies.name: Narrow port
supported_topologies.description: A port with a single phy.

supported_topologies.name: Wide port
supported_topologies.description: A port with multiple phys sharing one SAS address; a wide link connects two wide ports.

supported_topologies.name: Edge expander
supported_topologies.description: Connects end devices; an edge expander set bounds a subtractive routing domain.

supported_topologies.name: Fanout expander
supported_topologies.description: Connects multiple edge expander devices to build large topologies.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Originates SSP/STP/SMP connection requests and SCSI commands (e.g. an HBA).
Responds to commands (e.g. a SAS drive); has an SSP target port and logical units.
Routes connections among phys; contains the SMP target function and the expander route table.
Bridges tunneled SATA traffic to a SATA device behind an expander.

fields.interconnect_role: SAS is a serial storage fabric. Connections are opened on demand between ports identified by 64-bit SAS addresses; expanders route them (table / subtractive / direct). Wide ports provide aggregate bandwidth and path redundancy. SSP carries SCSI, STP tunnels SATA, and SMP manages the topology.

ordering_guarantees.connection: A connection is a dedicated full-duplex path until CLOSE; frames are ordered within the connection.
ordering_guarantees.wide_port: Connections may be spread across the phys of a wide port.
ordering_guarantees.arbitration: Contention is resolved by arbitration wait time across the SAS domain.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: SAS is not memory-mapped; connections and frames are addressed by 64-bit SAS address (and SCSI LUN within an SSP target), not by a memory or peripheral address. Management uses SMP request/response.
